title: Cannabis Dispensary SOPs: Receiving Inventory
summary: Everything you need to know about receiving a delivery of cannabis products from a distributor in states like California, Massachusetts, New Jersey and Michigan
body_markdown:
Receiving cannabis inventory is the process of ordering product from a licensed distributor, verifying the delivery and its paperwork on arrival, accepting the transfer in Metrc, and building a purchase order in your POS before anything reaches the shelf. Do those steps out of order and you get the three problems every operator knows: inventory discrepancies, audit exposure, and product you cannot legally sell.


The cannabis industry keeps expanding, and with it the demand for well-organized, efficient dispensaries. Operating a dispensary means delegating tasks to a team of professionals who can handle a range of responsibilities. The best way to do that is by curating your own cannabis dispensary standard operating procedures, or Cannabis SOPs, and communicating those guidelines to your entire staff. New team members especially appreciate well-documented step-by-step instructions to reference during onboarding.


**This is a complete guide to product intake and deliveries in Metrc states, covering ordering, security, paperwork, receiving through Metrc, and building the purchase order. Every step is written so a new hire can follow it on their first shift.**

## Order Products


The first step in receiving cannabis inventory is ordering product from licensed distributors. Make sure you are stocking licensed brands that meet the requirements set by state and local government agencies. Cannabis products must pass a quality assessment, be lab tested, meet child-resistant and general packaging requirements, and be tracked in Metrc.


Once those products and brands are verified, place your initial order with your distributor. Ordering based on reliable data is critical whether you are a new dispensary or an experienced buyer.


### Your First Orders as a New Dispensary


**For new dispensaries** , it is essential to choose brands carefully, accounting for the competition and the local market. When you are launching, you have an idea of your customer but you do not yet know who your audience will actually be. Review what other brands and price points are available from dispensaries and delivery services nearby, and use that to make educated guesses about what to stock first.


To create a balanced menu, understand the customer base and demographics you serve, and select brands and distributors that meet their needs. Research the products available locally and compare them against your target demographic. Make sure the products you order align with your brand identity.


Do not overstock at the beginning. Purchase only enough for the initial orders until sales increase. After that first purchase, monitor sales with analytics and ordering velocity tools to identify your best performing products, then use that data to make sure you never run out of them. ## Schedule the Delivery with the Distributor


Scheduling the arrival of inventory matters, but so does recording what you ordered and when it is expected. Maintaining an accurate, up-to-date record of inventory on order is essential to running the floor well, and it saves your staff the headache of planning a day around a delivery nobody logged.


---


## Delivery Procedures


### Verify the Identity of the Delivery Driver Upon Arrival


Keep a sign-in book for drivers so you can monitor who enters and exits your shop. It is a simple, effective way to confirm that deliveries were made on time by authorized personnel, and it gives you something to reference later if a discrepancy surfaces. Most dispensaries have a policy of assigning drivers a guest badge to stay compliant with their state cannabis control agency. Issue the badge, and make sure the driver signs in.


### Security Measures


Dispensary safety is critical when checking in a delivery, especially if cash handling is involved. **Can anyone walk into your shop if they claim they are dropping off a delivery?** Verify the identity of the delivery person and set a policy for having security present while product is counted. Staff training and inventory monitoring matter here too. Prioritizing security protects your staff, your customers, and your business from preventable losses.


Read more:[How to Build a Dispensary Security Plan](https://getmeadow.com/blog/dispensary-security-plan)


### Confirm Required Paperwork


Cannabis is an intensely regulated industry. Before receiving a delivery, refer to your state and local regulations. Most delivery rules involve required paperwork covering transporter details and Metrc tag information.


California, Michigan, Massachusetts, and New Jersey all require a shipping manifest that includes information about the cannabis being transported, along with the names and registration numbers of the dispensary agents involved. All four require transporters to hold a valid license issued by the regulatory authority overseeing cannabis in that state. They must also use a manifest meeting state-specific requirements, which generally include the businesses involved in the transport, the personnel, the date and time of departure and arrival, the quantity and description of the products, the license plate and vehicle description, and the route. Each of these states requires transporters to comply with Metrc. If the driver does not have the proper paperwork on hand, you cannot compliantly receive the product.


These states also require Certificates of Analysis, or COAs, to be uploaded to Metrc for transparency, and Metrc tags must be used to track the movement of the cannabis. Make sure the driver has these documents prepared on arrival, and that they are accurate.

## Count and Inspect All Products from the Distributor


Take your time here. The quality assessment is one of the most important steps in the process. Inspect and count the product to confirm the Metrc paperwork is correct. Once confirmed, make sure the Metrc manifest, the invoice, and the physical quantities all match.


### More on Quality Control


Things to look for during your quality assessment:


- Check for any damaged packaging.
- Verify the packaging meets child-resistant requirements and other state-regulated standards.
- Confirm the product's expiration date. Set a standard in your SOP for how close to expiration you are willing to accept a product. The closer it is to expiring, the less time you have to sell it and make margin before it has to be destroyed.


Following these steps keeps your dispensary compliant with state law and puts safe, high-quality product in front of your customers. Never receive a package in Metrc without confirming these details first. Doing so puts your dispensary at risk.

## Final Inspection of the Invoice and Sign Off


Once you have inspected and verified the product, confirm the cost per unit is accurate and matches the agreed-upon rate. Check that no additional product has been included that could throw off your inventory counts. This step prevents compliance and accounting problems later.


If any vendor reimbursements or credits are due, make sure they appear on the invoice, and notify the supplier of any discrepancies. Both the driver and your employee need to sign the Metrc manifest, confirming receipt of the product and acknowledging that all checks and inspections are complete. Done consistently, this is what keeps inventory counts accurate, your dispensary compliant, and the supply chain intact.


---


## Confirm Payment Terms


Next, determine whether payment is due for the received product. When handling cash payments, signed paperwork is a must for transparency and record-keeping accuracy. A money counter streamlines the process and reduces errors. If you are on net terms with your supplier, schedule a payment pick-up as soon as possible to avoid service interruptions. Update your records and accounting system to reflect the payment, and confirm it aligns with the received product's cost and quantity.


---


## Receive the Inventory Transfer in Metrc


After completing all checks and inspections, confirm that the electronic Metrc transfer matches both the manifest and the physical inventory before you receive it. This is what keeps inventory counts accurate and your dispensary compliant. If anything does not match, contact the supplier immediately. Once everything reconciles, use Metrc to intake the products into your point of sale software.


This is the step where the wrong software costs you. ## Cannabis Inventory Receiving FAQs


### What paperwork do you need to receive a cannabis delivery?


At minimum, a shipping manifest that meets your state's requirements, a valid transporter license, and the Metrc tag information for the packages being delivered. In California, Michigan, Massachusetts, and New Jersey, the manifest generally must include the businesses involved, the personnel, departure and arrival times, the quantity and description of the products, the vehicle description and license plate, and the route. Certificates of Analysis must also be uploaded to Metrc. If the driver does not have this documentation on hand and accurate, you cannot compliantly receive the product.


### What should you check before accepting a cannabis delivery?


Count the product and inspect it before anything else. Confirm the Metrc manifest, the invoice, and the physical quantities all match. Check for damaged packaging, verify child-resistant and state packaging requirements, and confirm expiration dates against the threshold set in your SOP.


### Can you receive a Metrc transfer before counting the product?


No. Never receive a package in Metrc before confirming the physical count, the manifest, and the invoice all agree. Accepting the transfer first means you have attested to quantities you have not verified, and correcting it afterward creates the discrepancy trail auditors look for.


### Which states require Metrc for receiving cannabis inventory?


All six states Meadow serves run on Metrc: California, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, New Jersey, and New York. Manifest contents, transporter licensing, and COA requirements vary by state, so confirm the specifics for your market.


### Who signs off on a cannabis delivery?


Both the delivery driver and your receiving employee sign the Metrc manifest. That signature confirms receipt of the product and acknowledges that all checks and inspections are complete, which is why it comes last rather than on arrival.
